target_scope: Exact finite-horizon first-hit probability on the inherited Euler grid; p0=4.304224792713203e-10 is a source-reported estimate used only as a planning scale.

claims.claim: For Q=epsilon P+(1-epsilon)Qc on complete stopped paths, Y=1_A dP/dQ is unbiased for p, bounded by 1/epsilon, and has second moment at most p/epsilon.

The inverted two-sided Bernstein interval is computable from observed mean x, n, epsilon and delta; at the inherited probability scale and 20.84M-force budget it is vacuous even under generous sample-count assumptions.

A rare-spike subclass of [0,1/epsilon] variables forces at least (1-2delta)/(3 r epsilon p0) samples to distinguish two disjoint relative-r intervals, so no method using only the range can close the budget gate.
Mixing P and Qc separately at each Euler step compounds the path likelihood envelope to epsilon^(-tau), at most epsilon^(-4000).

The inherited clipped control |u|<=80 gives the finite but useless Qc second-moment envelope exp(6400) at T=2, and an energy-only truncation bias bound needs a likelihood cap above 10^1629.79 at the p0 scale.

A positive finite-horizon approximate committor g with certified one-step ratios Z_k/g_k in exp(+-eta_k) yields an event-scale path-weight envelope Y<=exp(2h) p for h=sum eta_k; the exact h-transform has zero variance.

The inherited 10,000-path empirical SE and observed maximum remain diagnostics, not a finite-sample probability certificate; the current result does not establish a stationary rate, continuous-time rate, atomistic result, or mission completion.
